daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Democratic Party is holding its 25th anniversary celebration today, with President Prabowo invited and AHY calling on party cadres to prepare for the 2029 elections. The event comes days after AHY's speech about power having limits triggered reactions from pro-Prabowo parties, prompting the Democratic Party to issue clarifications, while analysts debate the speech's impact on Prabowo's coalition and the 2029 presidential race. A Parameter Politik Indonesia survey found that 80.2 percent of respondents want PDI-P to remain in opposition.

  • Parliament has summoned a major marketplace over frozen vendor funds, marking an escalation in DPR oversight of digital commerce platforms.
  • A student group has challenged the sorcery article in the new Criminal Code before the Constitutional Court.
  • Corruption suspect Silmy Karim is contesting the KPK's asset seizure in his case.
  • A Kemenag employee testified that hajj acceleration fees first emerged during Minister Yaqut's tenure, while investigators revealed that "Para Gus" and DPR members received additional hajj quota allocations.
  • North Sumatra Governor Masinton vowed not to resign amid impeachment discussions, saying he will respect the people's choice.
  • A Parameter survey showed that the majority of the public supports asset confiscation from convicted corruptors.
  • Media personality Aldi Taher and several influencers joined the Democratic Party.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia received support from 180 Japanese troops to fight forest fires, with Japan also deploying three helicopters for wildfire response. Upon arrival in Indonesian waters, Italian carrier Garibaldi was immediately deployed for forest fire operations. The bilateral cooperation represents a significant military-to-military engagement as Indonesia battles extensive wildfire outbreaks across multiple provinces.

  • Indonesia and the United States expanded cooperation on AI and child online protection.
  • A sports minister proposed using pencak silat as a bridge to strengthen Indonesia-Japan sports ties.
  • Police foiled the smuggling of Rp 4.6 billion worth of shrimp fry from Sidoarjo to Singapore.

Other

The government has restructured Whoosh high-speed rail debt to US$56 million in annual installments, with the Finance Ministry taking over the obligation from PT KCIC. The debt restructuring, detailed in four key facts, represents a major fiscal adjustment for Indonesia's flagship rail project. The Finance Minister separately urged regional governments to assess risks before issuing bonds.

  • The government announced that the E20 bioethanol mandate is targeted to take effect in 2028, while companies violating B50 biodiesel obligations face sanctions including license revocation, as the B50 program is projected to save Rp 170 trillion in foreign exchange.
  • Indonesia's PISA 2025 scores jumped significantly even as global scores declined.
  • BMKG explained that a newly discovered active fault in Surabaya has the potential to generate a magnitude 6.7 earthquake, urging residents to remain calm but vigilant.
  • Search and rescue teams expanded the search area for five missing journalists near Anak Krakatau, with Antara leading a joint team looking for the photojournalists as Mount Anak Krakatau erupted again today for 28 seconds.
  • The Environment Ministry urged regional governments to prepare for landfill fires due to extreme heat and revealed the causes of recent fires at Putri Cempo and Galuga landfills, while the Forestry Minister sealed burned forest land in West Kalimantan where palm oil planting had already begun.
  • BPS clarified that DTSEN is not a social assistance recipient list, addressing confusion over the integrated social welfare data system.
